name: Custom
summary: A slot for a component the host implements itself: a logo, a brand moment, a bespoke widget. The document names it and gives it props; the product renders it, and a fallback stands in when it can't.

name.description: The host's name for the component, namespaced: 'brand.logo', 'store.map'

props.description: What the host component takes; values may be bindings

fallback.description: What renders when the host has no component of that name: a Text, a Media, a Status. Required, so the document stands on its own

label.description: An accessible name for the slot when the host component is decorative or complex

whenToUse: The parts of a product that are truly its own: a logo, an illustration system, a map, a chart type the spec doesn't have
Only in authored documents: a shell or a screen a person wrote for that product
whenNotToUse: Anything a spec component can express: a Custom is invisible to the verifier beyond its fallback
In a generated document: a generator can't know a host's components (the validator refuses it)

accessibility.role: whatever the host component provides; the fallback carries its own
requirements: The host component is responsible for its own accessibility; the verifier audits the rendered result
A decorative Custom is hidden from assistive tech; a meaningful one has a name

agent: Reads the host component if it exposes a role and name; otherwise reads the fallback.
rendering: The renderer looks the name up in the host's registry (the same one that overrides components); found, it renders it with the resolved props
Not found, it renders the fallback and notes the missing name in development
sources: Server-driven UI practice: escape hatches with fallbacks
